questions.prompt: Why is a normal external stylesheet render-blocking?

options.text: Because CSS files are always huge
Because the browser won't paint content until it has built the CSSOM from all applicable CSS
Because CSS must run before JavaScript

questions.explanation: The browser needs the CSSOM before painting, so an applicable stylesheet blocks the first paint until it's downloaded and parsed — a big part of LCP's render-delay phase.

questions.prompt: Which techniques keep resources off the critical path? Select all that apply.

options.text: Inline critical CSS and load the rest asynchronously
Inline the entire stylesheet into every HTML page

questions.explanation: Inlining critical CSS, scoping non-matching CSS with media, and deferring scripts all unblock the first paint. Inlining all CSS bloats HTML and loses caching.

questions.prompt: The minimal set of above-the-fold styles you inline so the first paint doesn't wait on a request is called ____ CSS.
questions.explanation: Critical CSS is the small above-the-fold style set inlined in the head; the full stylesheet is then loaded asynchronously.

questions.prompt: Match each technique to its effect.

pairs.right: First paint doesn't wait on a stylesheet request
It downloads without blocking the screen render
Runs after parsing, in document order
Runs as soon as it downloads, order not guaranteed

questions.explanation: Inlining critical CSS and scoping non-matching CSS unblock painting; defer/async keep scripts from blocking the parser.

questions.prompt: Why is inlining ALL of your CSS into the HTML a bad idea?

options.text: Inline CSS doesn't work in browsers
It bloats every HTML response, can't be cached separately, and is re-sent on every navigation
It forces the page to use dark mode

questions.explanation: Only the small critical set should be inlined. Inlining everything makes each HTML response large and uncacheable, hurting multi-page visits.

questions.prompt: Order the timeline of an optimized, non-blocking head as the page paints.

items.text: Inline critical CSS lets the browser paint above-the-fold
The full stylesheet finishes loading asynchronously and applies
The deferred script runs after parsing

questions.explanation: With critical CSS inline and the rest async plus a deferred script, the browser paints early and the non-critical resources apply/run off the critical path.
